_what: One self-check set written with every interactive task type (2.74.0) - Part A (check what was taught) first, then Part B (find it yourself). A builder copies a question, keeps the shape and writes the course's own words. Demo content (LPG cargo): every figure is checked against the course KB before use. The 3D scenes and build-sheet entries beside this file are the starting points for a deck, a room and a valve.

screens.title: Self-check 2 - cargo hazards
screens.text:
Self-check on your tablet now.
Part A first, then Part B.

screens.question: True or false? Flick each card.
screens.answer:
Propane vapour is heavier than air and collects in low places* => Its vapour is about 1.5 times as heavy as air.
LPG boils at a higher temperature than water => Propane boils at about -42 °C.
Warm methane vapour is lighter than air* => Its density is about 0.55 of air's once warm.
A reading of 0 % LEL means a tank is safe to enter => Oxygen and toxic gas must be measured too.
screens.feedback: Heavy propane, cold LPG, light warm methane, and never only the LEL.
screens.brief: Think about what each gas does when it leaks.

screens.question: At atmospheric pressure, propane boils at about…
screens.brief: That is the boiling point of another cargo.

screens.question: The detector, calibrated for propane, shows a steady reading. What is the gas concentration in % by volume?
screens.answer:
0.84 % vol ± 0.02
! EX · PROPANE: 40 % LEL
# Gas | LEL, % vol | UEL, % vol
# Propane | 2.1 | 9.5
# Butane | 1.8 | 8.4
# Methane | 5.0 | 15.0
screens.brief: Check which number you took from the data sheet, and the unit.

screens.question: A propane tank is at 0 °C and 4.7 bar. The cargo warms to +40 °C. Where will the pressure be?
screens.feedback: About 13.7 bar - vapour pressure climbs faster as the cargo warms.
screens.brief: Pressure does not rise in a straight line.

screens.question: Use the test rig to answer both challenges.
screens.answer:
find: A mixture that burns with methane but will not burn with propane => x > 9.5 and x <= 15
find: With the detector covered, set propane to what it would read as 50 % LEL => Propane; 0.95 <= x <= 1.15; hide Detector
screens.feedback: Methane burns 5-15 %, propane 2.1-9.5 %; 50 % LEL of propane is 1.05 %.
screens.brief: Spark both gases at the same mixture.

screens.question: 06:10 - the gas alarm sounds in the compressor room. Open the sources, pin the evidence, then say what happened.
options: A leak at the compressor 2 flange; heavy vapour pools low because extraction stopped
The floor detector head is faulty
Normal vapour after loading that will clear by itself
screens.answer:
LOG | Gas detection log: Time | Floor | Upper ;; 05:40 | 2 % LEL | 0 ;; 06:10 | 35 % LEL ALARM | 4 *
DATA | Cargo data sheet: Vapour density | 1.55 (air = 1) *
ROUND | Deck round note: Frost and a hiss at the compressor 2 suction flange *
ENGINE | Engine room log: 05:50 extraction fan 1 tripped, not restarted *
WX | Weather report: Wind NW 12 kn, air 14 °C
screens.feedback: Floor ≫ upper, heavy vapour, frost at the flange, the fan stopped.
screens.brief: Some of what you pinned does not explain the alarm, or the conclusion does not fit it.

screens.question: The duty officer posted this before the watch. Keep each sentence that is right; correct the ones that are wrong.
screens.answer:
Propane is lighter than air, so a leak on deck rises and clears away => Propane vapour is heavier than air and collects low* | Propane is lighter than air only when cold
If a cargo tank warms up, the pressure inside it rises => * | The pressure falls as it warms | The pressure stays the same - the tank is closed
Butane boils at -42 °C, the same as propane => Butane boils at about -0.5 °C* | Butane boils at about -162 °C
screens.feedback: Heavy propane, pressure up with heat, butane at -0.5 °C.
screens.brief: Not every claim that sounds wrong is wrong.

screens.question: You take over the watch. Discharge tank 2 to shore through the port manifold; keep tank 1 out of the line.
screens.answer:
goal: Tank 2 => Port manifold
keep out: Tank 1; Starboard manifold
V101: Tank 1 valve = open
V201: Header valve, tank 1 side = open
V102: Tank 2 valve = shut
V202: Header valve, tank 2 side = shut
V301: Port manifold valve = shut
V302: Starboard manifold valve = open
screens.feedback: Open V102, V202, V301; shut V302 and V201 (or V101).
screens.brief: Follow the cargo from the pump - where else can it go?

screens.question: Morning round in the compressor room. There are 4 problems - find them.
screens.answer:
Compressor suction line: frost on the flange, a faint hiss, mist sinking to the floor*
Portable work lamp: an ordinary 230 V lamp, no Ex marking, plugged in*
Gas detector head, floor level: a red plastic cap over its inlet*
Extraction fan No. 1: STOPPED lamp lit, the blades still*
Dry powder extinguisher: in its bracket, seal unbroken, needle in the green
Compressor suction gauge: 0.2 bar, inside the 0-0.5 bar on its placard
Emergency stop: guard closed, button out
Cargo compressor No. 2: stopped, casing dry
Drip tray: dry and clean
screens.feedback: The leak, the non-Ex lamp, the capped detector, the stopped fan.
screens.brief: Look low as well as high.

screens.question: Take the ball valve apart and find out how it works.
screens.answer:
part: Cargo pipe: carbon steel, 100 mm bore
part: Flange joint: two flanges, a gasket and eight bolts
part: Valve body: cast steel; the stem comes out through its top
part: Ball: a steel sphere with a round hole through it
part: Seat rings: PTFE, one each side of the ball, pressed against it
part: Stem: a steel shaft from the ball up to the handle
part: Gland packing: graphite rings round the stem under a hexagon nut
part: Handle: a steel lever; it moves a quarter turn
find: Which part stops cargo getting past the ball when the valve is closed? => Seat rings
find: Which part stops cargo leaking out along the stem? => Gland packing
set: Close the valve => closed
screens.feedback: Seats seal the ball, the gland seals the stem, across the pipe is closed.
screens.brief: Pull it apart and look at what touches what.

screens.question: Tank 2 has been gas-freed and ventilated. Test the atmosphere before anyone goes in.
screens.feedback: Top, middle and bottom, each after the sample arrived.
screens.brief: A reading only counts once the sample has come up the hose - and the air is layered.

screens.question: From your readings: can anyone go into tank 2?
options: Yes - the readings near the hatch are fine
Yes, with a filter mask on
No - keep ventilating, then test every level again
screens.feedback: The bottom failed on oxygen and on LEL.
screens.brief: Look at every level you tested, not only one.
